To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
income differences among designers are mainly determined by business experience, the use of ICT and networking.

(i) income of designers is determined mainly by their business experience and the extent to which they use ICTs, (ii) spatial clustering and networking do not have an impact on designers' incomes, and (iii) the education of designers has no effect on their income.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the design sector in the creative economy, the income differences among designers and the role of spatial clustering in fostering the success of designers.
the income differences of designers and the role of spatial clustering in fostering regional development.
the role of the design sector in the creative economy and with the role of design entrepreneurs in the creative class.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the design sector in the Netherlands is a sector where a lot of people are working, but not necessarily earning a lot of money.
the Dutch design industry is a very competitive environment.
the creative class is a very heterogeneous group of people.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
design is a profession in which experience is the most important asset.
the Dutch design sector is a highly competitive sector with many small firms.

the design sector is a sector of the creative economy where the creative capital of individuals, in the form of experience and ICTs, is the main determinant of success, rather than the spatial concentration of creative individuals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the creative class is a heterogeneous group of individuals with varying levels of success.
the design sector in general is not a good target for regional development policy.
policy makers should not only focus on regional development but also on the development of the individual designer and the firm.
